$comment: Reviewed, time-boxed advisory ignores for `pnpm audit --audit-level=high`. Each entry MUST have a reason and an expiry; CI fails any entry past expiry so ignores can't rot. Empty by default - add only un-fixable transitive advisories. Swept 2026-08-19: every advisory with a published patched version was fixed by a bump or a pnpm override (see pnpm-workspace.yaml), which took high+critical from 51 findings / 44 blocking down to the 8 below. Five entries were DELETED rather than renewed because the advisories they covered are no longer reported at all: 1119610 and 1120729 (tmp - superseded, and the testcontainers copy is now overridden to 0.2.7), 1120679 (esbuild), 1120791 (vite - superseded by 1123527, fixed by vite 8.0.16), 1120799 (protobufjs - superseded by 1123488). The two remaining chains share one expiry, 2026-11-30, because they also share one re-review: each is blocked on a named upstream change, not on anything Cairn can bump.

ignores.reason: DEV/BUILD-INPUT ONLY, not request-reachable. Pinned at 6.11.6 by @xenova/transformers -> onnxruntime-web -> onnx-proto@4.0.4 (declares ^6.11.2 - won't accept v7). A pnpm override to v7 silently fails because onnx-proto's compiled pbjs output targets the v6 API. The advisory is RCE via protobufjs decode of attacker-controlled wire bytes; the only protobuf inputs in this codebase are the bundled ONNX embedding models (operator-controlled, fetched at build by scripts/fetch-embedding-assets.mjs). No untrusted protobuf wire traffic reaches the library. EXIT: migrate off the unmaintained @xenova/transformers@2 to @huggingface/transformers@4, whose onnxruntime-web dependency has no onnx-proto and therefore no protobufjs 6.x pin. That is a code migration, not a bump, which is why it is time-boxed rather than done here.

Same onnx-proto chain and same exit as 1117571. Code injection through bytes-field defaults in generated toObject - requires attacker control over the protobuf SCHEMA, not the wire bytes. No untrusted schemas in this codebase (bundled ONNX models only).

Same onnx-proto chain and same exit as 1117571. Code-generation gadget after prototype pollution - requires a prior prototype-pollution primitive plus attacker control over the schema. Bundled ONNX models only.

Same onnx-proto chain and same exit as 1117571. Process-wide DoS through unsafe option paths in protobufjs codegen. Requires attacker control over option paths in the schema. Bundled ONNX models only.
Same onnx-proto chain and same exit as 1117571. DoS through unbounded protobuf recursion in decode. Wire-byte input only - no untrusted protobuf wire traffic reaches this library in this codebase.

NEW 2026-08-19, same onnx-proto chain and same exit as 1117571 (it replaces the superseded 1120799). DoS through unbounded Any expansion during protobuf JSON conversion; requires attacker-controlled protobuf JSON input, and the only protobuf inputs here are the bundled ONNX model files. Patched in protobufjs >=7.6.1, which the v6-API-bound onnx-proto still cannot accept.

DEV-ONLY. Now scoped to @lhci/cli@0.15.1 alone: tmp@0.0.33 via inquirer@6.5.2 -> external-editor@3.1.0, and tmp@0.1.0 as a direct @lhci/cli dep. Lighthouse CI runs the perf-budget check in CI and never ships in the production bundle. The advisory is path traversal via unsanitized prefix/postfix to tmp.dirSync/fileSync; @lhci/cli never passes user-controlled values to those calls. The testcontainers copy that used to appear under this class is now forced to 0.2.7 by a pnpm override, so this entry no longer covers it. EXIT: @lhci/cli shipping a release that upgrades its tmp/inquirer chain - 0.15.1 is still the latest published version as of 2026-08-19.

DEV-ONLY and UNPATCHABLE TODAY - there is no fixed release to bump to. The advisory says patched >=2.0.2 but 2.0.1 is still the newest version published to npm as of 2026-08-19, so no override can clear it. Reached only through @lhci/cli -> lighthouse -> puppeteer-core -> @puppeteer/browsers, i.e. the CI perf-budget tool unpacking Chrome builds it downloaded itself; the vulnerable path is a symlink escape from a zip, and the only zips involved are Google's Chrome-for-Testing archives. Never present in the production bundle. EXIT: @puppeteer/browsers@3.x already dropped extract-zip entirely (it uses modern-tar), so this clears as soon as @lhci/cli bumps lighthouse/puppeteer-core - or immediately if extract-zip 2.0.2 is ever published.
